transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess… work is the main reason. I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch before all the approvals were actually in place. I committed company money and vendor time, and at the time it felt like the right move—bold, necessary.

Now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking. So… that’s why I’m here.
After the work incident, did you experience a period where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually care about?
I don’t know. I mean… I’ve been stressed and embarrassed about it, sure. But “hopeless” or not caring about things… I’m not sure I’d put it that way.
After the incident at work, did you feel unusually high, overly confident, or more energetic than usual for a period of time?

Yeah… I guess so. For the past few weeks I felt really… switched on. Like I could finally show leadership what HR should be.

But it wasn’t all positive. If someone questioned me—even small edits or budget stuff—I’d get furious pretty fast. More than I probably should have.
Can you describe how long you felt unusually high, confident, or energized? Was this a distinct period that lasted for days or even weeks?

It was… not just a day or two. Maybe about a month, building up.

It started around when the new executive came in and began pushing back on my onboarding redesign. That’s when I felt like I had to prove it could work.
During that time when you felt really switched on and energized, did you also feel like you didn't need much sleep, or that your thoughts were racing faster than usual?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I was keyed up, yeah, but I didn’t exactly track my sleep or anything. My mind was busy, I guess… but I don’t know if I’d call it racing.
During that time when you felt really energized and switched on, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual—like you could function well on just a few hours of sleep?
I don’t really know. I mean… maybe I slept a bit less some nights, but I can’t say I was fine on just a few hours or anything. I wasn’t paying that close attention.
Looking back at that time when you felt really energized and switched on, did you notice that you actually needed less sleep—like you could get by on fewer hours than usual and still feel rested?
I can’t really say that, no. I don’t remember feeling rested on less sleep. I just remember being worked up and focused, but the sleep part is… kind of blurry.

During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you notice that you could function normally even if you slept a lot less than usual—like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep?
No, I don’t think I can say that. I might’ve slept less here and there, but I don’t remember feeling rested or normal on just a few hours.
During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you feel like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual—like you could get by with a lot less sleep and still feel okay?
I don’t really remember it that way. Maybe I was up more, but I can’t say I felt fine or rested on less sleep.

During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you actually feel that you didn’t need much sleep at all—like you could stay up late and still be ready for the day without feeling tired?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember feeling like I didn’t need sleep. Maybe I stayed up later, but I can’t say I woke up ready to go or anything like that.

During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you actually feel like you didn’t need much sleep at all—like you could stay up late and still feel ready for the day without getting tired?
I don’t really know. I remember being up later sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I felt like I didn’t need sleep or anything.
During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you also feel unusually happy, elated, or unusually irritable most of the time?

Yeah… I guess so. For the past few weeks I’ve felt really alive, like I could finally show people at work what I can do. But I’ve also been getting angry pretty fast when someone questions me, even about small stuff.

During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you notice that you actually needed less sleep than usual—like you could get by with fewer hours of sleep and still feel rested and ready to go?
I don’t think so… I mean, I may have slept a little less here and there, but I wouldn’t say I felt rested or like I didn’t need sleep.
During the time you felt really energized and focused, did you actually feel like you needed less sleep than usual—like you could sleep just a few hours and still feel rested?
No… not really. I’ve been up late a few times, but I don’t remember feeling rested on just a few hours.

During that time when you felt really energized and focused, did you actually feel like you didn’t need much sleep at all—like you could stay up late and still feel ready for the day without getting tired?
I don’t think so. I mean, I stayed up later sometimes, but not like I could just skip sleep and be fine.
Looking back, would you say that during that time you actually felt like you didn’t need much sleep at all—like you could stay up late and still feel ready for the day without getting tired?
Not really, no. I don’t remember it that way. I might’ve been up late, but I wouldn’t say I felt like I didn’t need sleep.

During that time when you felt really energized and irritable, did you also notice that you were much more involved in work or other activities—like taking on more than usual or pushing harder than before?

Yeah… I guess I was taking on a lot. I was trying to run the HR redesign, reach out to gallery partners, contact festival people, and deal with a few staff conflicts all at the same time. It felt like if I had an idea, I needed to move on it right away.

Looking back at that time when you felt so energized and focused, did you actually feel like you didn’t need much sleep at all—like you could stay up late and still feel ready for the day without getting tired?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I stayed up late here and there, but I don’t remember feeling like I could just go without sleep and be fine.

Looking back, would you say that during this time of feeling energized and irritable, you were doing significantly more work or other activities than usual—like starting lots of projects, making a lot of plans, or pushing yourself much harder than before?

Yeah… I mean, I was definitely doing more than usual. I was trying to handle the HR redesign, line up gallery contacts, reach out to festival organizers, and smooth over staff issues all at the same time. It felt like once an idea came up, I had to act on it right then.
